reasons.arrivals: Not published: on the sealed seasons the model beat the base rate (log-loss gain 0.0637, 95% CI 0.0492 to 0.0782) but missed the calibration rule: it predicted 56.0% and 63.9% happened (tolerance 6.4 points; slope 0.964). The league base rate is shown instead.
reasons.type: The type split did not beat the training shares on the sealed seasons: the shares are shown.
reasons.targets: The target ranking did not beat both the need x value ranking and chance on the sealed seasons.

notes: Chance of moving: a ridge logistic regression on our own movement history (nflverse weekly rosters 2002 on: who was listed where each week), refitted each season and validated on held-out seasons (Model page).

No contract data: salaries, cap figures and contract years are not used, because no source whose terms allow our use has them (OverTheCap's terms; nflverse's contracts table is OverTheCap's). Free agency is inferred from age, accrued seasons (a rookie deal runs four), draft slot, tenure with the team and role.
Traded or claimed: the weekly rosters cannot tell a trade from a waiver claim. The offseason is not seen week by week, so free agency, offseason cuts and offseason trades are one type.
Value is Gridiron value (points above replacement), the last two seasons blended 3:2; offensive linemen are not valued individually, so they are never targets.

Outlook: the chance of adding at least one player at the position who was on another team's roster at the snapshot, by next season's week 1 (a Poisson model of past arrivals: need there, team strength and trajectory, turnover, expected departures).

Targets: players on other rosters who would upgrade the team's weakest starting slot at their position, ranked by their chance of joining it: the chance the player moves x the chance this team is where they go (a conditional logit on past moves). An estimate from on-field value and history, not news.
